# Track your monthly bills and spot unusual charges with ChatRTX

> **In short:** ChatRTX is a free NVIDIA app that runs an AI chatbot directly on your RTX graphics card. Load your bills as documents and ask it to summarize charges, flag unusual jumps, and suggest savings — all without sending your data to the cloud.

If you've ever stared at a long phone or electricity bill wondering "what is half of this stuff?", this guide is for you. We'll use ChatRTX to turn a stack of PDFs into a one-page summary, compare months side by side, and spot the kind of small but recurring charges that quietly add up over a year.

## Before you start
- An NVIDIA RTX graphics card (RTX 30-series or newer) with at least 8 GB of VRAM (the memory built into the graphics card). You can check this in **Task Manager → Performance → GPU** on Windows.
- A Windows 10 or 11 PC with about 15 GB of free disk space.
- ChatRTX downloaded and installed from NVIDIA's website. The installer is several gigabytes because it includes the AI model files (the AI's "brain" — think of it as a smart assistant that lives on your computer instead of on someone else's server).
- At least 2-3 monthly bills saved as readable PDFs or text files. Scanned image-only bills may not work without OCR (a tool that reads text out of images) first.
- About 20-30 minutes for the first setup. Later sessions are much faster.

## Step 1 — Install ChatRTX and open it for the first time
Download the ChatRTX installer from NVIDIA's site and double-click it. The installer first copies the app, then downloads a large language model — the actual AI that does the reading and answering. This second step can take a while on a slow connection, so plug in your laptop or grab a coffee. When it finishes, a window opens with a chat box at the bottom and a short welcome message.

If you don't see the welcome message, look for an icon on your desktop or in the Start menu labeled **ChatRTX** — NVIDIA sometimes places it there after installing.

You'll know it worked when the chat window is empty and waiting for you to type — that means the app is running and the AI model is fully loaded.

## Step 2 — Make a folder for your bills
On your desktop or inside your Documents folder, create a new folder called something simple like **Bills-2025**. Drop the PDFs or text versions of your bills into it. Each file should have a clear name like **electricity-july-2025.pdf** so the AI can tell them apart later when you ask about specific months. If your bill is a photo or a scanned image, ChatRTX will struggle to read it — in that case, copy the text out by hand or run it through a free OCR tool first (most phone scanning apps include one).

💬 Example: a clean folder with files named `phone-july.pdf`, `phone-august.pdf`, `streaming-august.pdf`, `electricity-august.pdf`.

You'll know it worked when every file in the folder opens and shows readable text — not just a picture of text.

## Step 3 — Point ChatRTX at your bills folder
In the ChatRTX window, look for a button or menu that says something like **Add documents**, **Dataset**, or a folder icon. Click it and pick the **Bills-2025** folder you just made. ChatRTX reads every file inside and builds a private search index — basically a quick-lookup table of everything in your bills. The first time you do this, it can take a minute or two per document, so don't worry if the app looks busy for a bit.

If you can't find that button, check the top menu bar or a **⋯** (three dots) icon in the corner — NVIDIA sometimes moves it between updates.

You'll know it worked when ChatRTX shows a message like "Documents loaded" or you see a small list of your file names appear somewhere in the app window.

## Step 4 — Ask for a one-page summary of one bill
Now the fun part. In the chat box at the bottom of the window, type a clear question about one bill. Start small — just one document, one question. ChatRTX reads your bills locally, which means your data never leaves your computer.

💬 Example: `Summarize my August electricity bill in one short paragraph. What's the total, and what are the three biggest charges?`

What happens next: the AI types out an answer in the chat. It usually takes 5-15 seconds the first time, and gets faster after the model has warmed up. If the answer feels too vague or too long, click back in the chat box and add a follow-up like "Make it even shorter — three sentences max."

You'll know it worked when the answer names actual numbers from your bill — a total amount, dates, and charge names that match what's on the PDF.

## Step 5 — Compare two months and flag what jumped
Once a single summary works, ask it to compare. This is where ChatRTX is most useful for bills: it can read multiple documents side by side and tell you what's different. Be specific about which months and which kind of charge you care about, because vague questions get vague answers.

💬 Example: `Compare my July and August phone bills. What charges went up the most? Is anything new or unusual that didn't appear in July?`

What happens next: the AI walks through both bills and points out changes. Sometimes it will say things like "international roaming fee: $0 in July, $42 in August" — exactly the kind of thing that's easy to miss when you scan a bill yourself.

If it answers "I don't have that information," check that both bill files are in the same folder you loaded in Step 3. If one is missing, add it and click the **Refresh** or **Reindex** button if you see one in the app.

You'll know it worked when the response names specific line items with dollar amounts and clearly says which month they came from.

## Step 6 — Ask for saving suggestions — then double-check them
Now ask ChatRTX to suggest realistic places to cut back. Be honest about your goal so the advice is useful and not generic.

💬 Example: `Based on my phone and streaming bills, where could I realistically save about $20 to $30 a month without canceling services I actually use?`

What happens next: the AI gives you 3-5 suggestions pulled directly from your bill data — things like "you have a premium add-on that isn't showing usage" or "your data usage is well under your plan cap, so a smaller plan would work." Read each one with a healthy dose of skepticism, though. ChatRTX can only see your bills, not your actual life — it doesn't know that your teenager uses 80 GB of mobile data "just in case," or that you actually watch that niche streaming service every weekend.

You'll know it worked when the suggestions are tied to specific charges on your bills, not vague advice like "consider switching providers" with no numbers attached.

## Common mistakes
- **Loading image-only scanned PDFs.** ChatRTX reads text, not pictures of text. If your bill is a photo, run it through a free OCR tool (many phone scanning apps have one built in) before loading it.
- **Asking one giant question.** "Analyze all my bills and tell me everything" overwhelms the AI and gives a fuzzy answer. Break it into one bill, one month, one question at a time — the AI does better in small steps.
- **Trusting the savings tips blindly.** ChatRTX only sees what's in the documents you gave it. It cannot know your full budget, family size, or which subscriptions matter to you. Treat its tips as conversation starters, not financial advice.
- **Forgetting the hardware.** ChatRTX is free but it needs a fairly new NVIDIA RTX graphics card. If your PC doesn't have one, the app simply won't run — check your GPU model in Task Manager before downloading anything.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** A 30-second chat every month can catch the mystery fee you missed — the random $9.99 charge that "renewed automatically" three months ago and you never noticed.
- **For your business or work:** Freelancers and small-business owners can drop a folder of software subscriptions into ChatRTX once a quarter and quickly see which tools you actually use and which ones are pure cost.
- **If you're just getting started:** Don't try to load ten bills at once. Pick the one bill that confuses you most — usually phone or cable — and run Steps 4 through 6 on it. You'll learn the rhythm before adding more.

## Try it now
Open ChatRTX, load your most recent phone bill, and ask it one simple question: `What's the single biggest charge on this bill, and is it something I asked for?` That single answer often pays back the time it took to set up the whole tool.
